issues.legal_issue: A decree for possession cannot be executed again after the decree-holder has accepted delivery of possession, even though the person bound by the decree remains physically on the property with the decree-holder’s permission.
material_facts: The decree required delivery of possession of property occupied by the judgment-debtor.
During execution, the decree-holder accepted delivery while allowing the judgment-debtor to remain on the property by permission.
The decree-holder gave a receipt acknowledging delivery of possession, and guards were placed on the property on the decree-holder’s behalf.

The execution record stated that possession had been delivered and the execution case was dismissed on part satisfaction, while recording that possession had been delivered as against this judgment-debtor.
The decree-holder later filed a fresh application seeking to remove the judgment-debtor from the property.
issues.conclusion: The decree had been fully executed as against the judgment-debtor, so it could not be executed again to obtain possession of the property.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21, Rule 35 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a person bound by a decree for possession is removed only if removal is necessary to give the decree-holder the possession sought. The decree-holder may accept delivery without the occupant’s physical removal; having accepted and acknowledged delivery, the decree-holder is bound by that position and cannot seek execution again. The Court followed Maharaja Jagadish Nath Roy v. Nafar Chandra Paramanik, (1930) 35 C.W.N. 12. The interlocutory order allowing time to vacate did not decide whether execution had already been completed and did not prevent the claim that it had.

rule.if: possession_decree_execution and decree_holder_accepted_delivery and occupant_remained_by_permission and delivery_acknowledged_as_complete and later_fresh_execution

predicates.possession_decree_execution: The proceeding seeks to execute a decree requiring delivery of possession of property.
predicates.decree_holder_accepted_delivery: The decree-holder accepted delivery of possession in the execution proceeding.
predicates.occupant_remained_by_permission: The person bound by the decree remained on the property with the decree-holder’s permission after delivery was accepted.
predicates.delivery_acknowledged_as_complete: The decree-holder acknowledged complete delivery, or the execution record recorded delivery as complete against that occupant.
predicates.later_fresh_execution: The decree-holder later sought a fresh execution to obtain possession already accepted as delivered.

issues.definition: When possession-decree execution results in accepted and acknowledged delivery, with the occupant remaining only by permission, a later fresh execution cannot obtain possession again.

issues.legal_issue: A person claiming through a party to an appeal may be added to the appeal to protect an interest acquired through that party.
material_facts: A company in possession of the property had granted mortgages over it to a bank.
The bank later obtained a mortgage decree, purchased the property at the mortgage sale, and took possession.
The bank conveyed the property and its interest to the proposed respondents while the appeal was pending.
The proposed respondents were added to the appeal, subject to the decree-holder’s right to object to their standing.
issues.conclusion: The proposed respondents were properly added to the appeal because they claimed through a party whose interest in the property was involved in the dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits proceedings to be taken by or against persons claiming under a party. An appeal is a proceeding for this purpose. Following Saila Bala Dassi v. Nirmala Sundari Dassi, [1958] S.C.R. 1287, the Court applied that principle to allow persons claiming through a party to be brought onto the appeal.

predicates.pending_appeal: An appeal is pending concerning rights or interests involved in the dispute.
predicates.applicant_claims_through_a_party: The applicant acquired or claims an interest through a party to the appeal or that party’s successor in interest.
predicates.applicant_seeks_to_participate_in_appeal: The applicant seeks to be added as a party to the pending appeal.

issues.definition: A person who claims through a party and seeks to participate in a pending appeal concerning that interest may be added to the appeal.
